Theme

Nature & food · Kitchen, meals & drinks

produce noun

fruit, vegetables and crops

also farm produce, fresh produce, local produce, crops

classical

Cic. Off. 2.12: frūgum frūctuumque reliquōrum perceptiō (Lewis & Short)
Varr. RR 1.23.1 (Lewis & Short)

frūctūs, frūctuum m. pl.

noun, fourth declension, plural

produce, the fruits of the land

Everything a field, an orchard or a herd yields; in the singular, a crop, or the profit from something. Fruit to eat is pōma (see fruit).

Other words

  • frūgēs, frūgum f. pl. — crops, the fruits of the earth (above all grain and pulses)

    noun, third declension, plural · also used · classical · Catull. 34.19–20: bonīs tēcta frūgibus explēs; Hor. Ep. 1.2.27: frūgēs cōnsūmere nātī; Traupman 166

    The dative frūgī is also the adjective “honest, thrifty” (see well-behaved).

Examples

  • vēr enim tamquam adulēscentiam significat ostenditque frūctūs futūrōs, reliqua autem tempora dēmetendīs frūctibus et percipiendīs accommodāta sunt

    for spring stands for youth, as it were, and shows the produce to come; the other seasons are suited to harvesting and gathering it inCic. Sen. 70

  • tū cursū, dea, mēnstruō mētiēns iter annuum, rūstica agricolae bonīs tēcta frūgibus explēs

    you, goddess, measuring out the year’s journey in your monthly course, fill the farmer’s country house with good cropsCatull. 34.17–20

See also fruit, vegetable, harvest, fruit stall, vegetable market, produce, crop.
